title: Redwood December 2026 All-Hands
summary: Quarter-end all-hands covering Q4 metrics, product roadmap adjustments, Dedicated & Private deployment updates, recent incident postmortem highlights, hiring plan for Q1, and company OKRs. Leadership recapped wins and asked teams to focus on reliability and cost-per-token improvements in the next quarter.
action_items: Ethan Park: Publish postmortem doc for Nov 30 outage by 2026-12-10
Maya Singh: Share updated Q1 roadmap slides with the company by 2026-12-09
Isabel Cruz: Distribute partner pricing playbook to GTM by 2026-12-14
Daniel Cho: Send performance tuning checklist for Dedicated to engineering managers by 2026-12-12
next_steps: Leadership to review Q1 hiring requests next week
Send recording and slides to all employees
Set up cross-functional reliability working group and first meeting before 2026-12-15
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-07 09:00 PT | Duration: 54 minutes | Location: All-hands - virtual
Attendees: Ava, Daniel, Maya, Ethan, Isabel, Liam + company

[00:00] Ava (CEO): Hey, everyone, good morning. Uh, thanks for joining the December all-hands. Quick housekeeping: recording is on, slides will be shared after. We'll keep this to about 50 minutes then some time for Q&A.

[00:18] Ava: First — big thank you. Q4 closed stronger than we expected, we beat our ARR targets and, uh, usage growth on hosted API is healthy. But we also had the outage last week which I know affected several customers, so we want to be transparent about that. Daniel will walk through the postmortem.

[01:05] Daniel (CTO): Thanks, Ava. Quick caveat, this is high-level, the full postmortem lives in the infra-docs repo, link in the follow-up email. Root cause: a cascade triggered by a bad autoscaling signal during a spike in prefix cache churn; KV cache thrashing caused node oom and rollout overlap with an older kernel. There was also an operator script that retried with exponential backoff but it raced with the autoscaler, so we ended up with more nodes than expected and then some OOMs.

[02:10] Daniel: Action that we took: immediate rollback of the canary config, rate-limited reintros, and we disabled the autoscale policy until we validated the telemetry. The longer-term fixes: a lock around the operator state, a safer default autoscale policy, and improved chaos testing for prefix cache workloads.

[03:12] Maya (Head of Product): Sorry to interrupt — question about the kernel mismatch you mentioned, is that the optimized attention kernel? There was some confusion in the support thread about whether it was model incompat or kernel version.

[03:30] Daniel: Good question. It was a kernel selection edge-case in the runtime's heuristics; when sequence lengths suddenly swung, the kernel selector picked a path that hadn't been exercised with recent quantized weights — so a memory regression. We're adding canary runs that specifically test those quantized variants.

[04:02] Ethan (VP Eng): From an engineering perspective, priority is reliability, then perf improvements that don't regress stability. I'm proposing we allocate a 20% of eng capacity for reliability work in Q1 — this includes observability improvements, replayable chaos tests, and autoscaler hardening.

[05:05] Ava: That sounds right. We also need to balance cost — customers keep asking about cost per token and predictable throughput. Isabel, any notes from sales on what customers are pushing on?

[05:25] Isabel (Head of Sales): Yes, two themes. One, enterprise accounts want stronger guarantees for Private/VPC deployments — SSO, RBAC, and longer retention of audit logs. Two, mid-market customers are very price sensitive; they ask about Dedicated reserved pricing vs hosted burst. We need clearer packaging. I'll work with product to get a partner playbook out.

[06:05] Ava: Good. On compliance, Liam and security team — where are we on SOC 2 and ISO?

[06:18] Liam (Head of People): Security and legal will cover SOC 2 gap list tomorrow. We're on track to submit for SOC 2 readiness review in January. ISO intake is queued, but we will prioritize SOC 2 first per customer asks. KMS integration for Private is in progress, and the HSM vendor discussions are late-stage.

[07:00] Daniel: One note — for Private deployments we need to make the KMS flow frictionless: key rollovers, multi-tenant key bindings, and audit hooks. We have a prototype but need to productize it in Q1.

[07:40] Maya: Roadmap adjustments. We are shifting one feature: the advanced batching UI will slip into Q2; the tradeoff we made is to accelerate Dedicated autoscale and the private KMS polish. Reason: customers told us the Dedicated predictability wins them procurement approvals faster.

[08:20] Maya: Also launching a new Optimize feature variant that gives recommendations for quantization profiles per workload — that's the one that can drive down unit cost without big latency hits. Demo planned for Jan.

[09:10] Ava: Thank you. Quick metrics block: growth — hosted API tokens up 28% Q/Q, Dedicated bookings up 5 new contracts this quarter, churn stable at 2.1%. Net retention improved but still below our target of 120% so that remains a focus.

[10:05] Ethan: On performance, the dedicated runtime benchmarks we ran with the 2.1 quantized models show a 1.8x throughput improvement but with some tail latency regressions in edge cases — those are the kernel-path issues Daniel mentioned. We'll be evaluating kernel selection heuristics and adding percentile-focused SLIs.

[11:00] Isabel: On go-to-market, we closed three mid-market logos using Dedicated pilot credits and a shortened procurement template. The legal team helped with the new master services addendum which cut procurement time by about two weeks.

[12:00] Ava: Hiring update — we ended Q4 with 152 people. Hiring freeze is not on the table, but we are being selective. We will prioritize infra, SRE, and product roles that directly improve reliability and cost optimization.

[12:30] Liam: We've also tightened interview loops for SRE to speed hiring — interview days will be weekly starting January. Equity refresh guidance for ICs will go out next week.

[13:05] Audience Q&A — pre-submitted question: "When will Dedicated get SLA-backed latency guarantees?"

[13:20] Ethan: We're working on a beta SLA for Dedicated targeted at next quarter. The initial offering will be availability and a latency window for common model profiles; we will require a sizing review to enforce the SLA.

[14:05] Audience Q: "Any changes to free credits or tiering for startups?"

[14:20] Isabel: We'll keep the current startup credits program but tighten the verification for high-usage accounts to avoid abuse. We're exploring an on-ramp for startups to Dedicated via a credit-backed pilot.

[15:05] Ava: Alright, let's do a short product demo preview — Maya?

[15:12] Maya: Quick screen share — (note: demo described, not real screen in transcript). Showing the new Optimize recommendations page: it suggests quantization levels, batching configurations, and caching TTLs based on workload profile. There's an experimental toggle to apply recommendations automatically. We will be conservative on auto-apply.

[17:25] Maya: Also rolling out per-route dashboards in Console so teams can see token-level cost and latency by model and route; this will help customers optimize faster without asking support.

[18:10] Audience comment (unlabeled): "Can we get more docs on prefix cache tuning?"

[18:20] Daniel: Yes, we'll publish a prefix cache tuning guide with examples for common traffic shapes. It's on the action items list.

[19:10] Ava: Quick finance update — burn is slightly under plan for the quarter, runway unchanged. Finance will share the detailed deck after this call. Big focus for next year is improving unit economics on tokens; revenue-side initiatives and cost-side (batching + quantization) will both contribute.

[20:03] Isabel: One note on partnerships: we're in talks with a big cloud partner for a managed private offering. Nothing signed yet but if it goes through it could materially expand APAC footprint.

[21:00] Q&A — question about open-source models and responsibilities: "Are we going to curate more open models?"

[21:15] Daniel: Yes, model catalog expansion continues. We will only onboard models we can verify performance and safety for; the onboarding includes an eval suite, perf profile, and suggested quantization. We reuse a lot of community tooling, but we run our own infra tests.

[22:05] Audience question: "What are the criteria for priority support?"

[22:20] Ava: Priority support will be part of the Dedicated/Enterprise offering; criteria include committed spend, mission-critical availability, and cadence for architecture reviews. We'll share a doc describing tiers next week.

[23:00] Ethan: Back to engineering priorities — I want to emphasize telemetry improvements: we need better token-level tracing into the serving runtime so we can attribute latency to kernel or IO. That will be a major project for Q1.

[24:05] Maya: Product will add quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets — this way if a model or quantization change causes output degradation, we get notified. That pairs with the Optimize tooling.

[25:00] Liam: Quick people note — holiday schedule and on-call rotations for end-of-year: please check the rota and request swaps early.

[25:40] Ava: Final recap and asks: 1) Publish postmortem and share with customers impacted; 2) Leadership to review Q1 roadmap and budget requests; 3) Set up reliability WG. Any final comments?

[26:05] Daniel: One last technical note — we'll spin up a canary cluster with traffic shaping to specifically reproduce the prefix churn patterns. Expect invites for follow-up sessions.

[26:30] Isabel: I'll coordinate with product for sales enablement material and updated pricing language for Dedicated.

[26:50] Ava: Thank you, all. We'll send slides, recording, and the action list. Happy holidays early, and let's finish strong.

[27:05] (Meeting ends; remaining minutes were used for small cross-team syncs and brief off-record follow-ups)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional mislabels and run-on sentences; speaker labels cleaned up where obvious. Some technical terms may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K-V cash", "HSM" as "H-S-M").
